summary: Adds a discount_code field and an apply_discount method to Order. Adds order detail and discount redeem endpoints.

findings.title: Order detail readable by any logged-in user
findings.problem: order_detail looks up the order by primary key only and never checks the owner. The redeem view in the same change does filter by owner=request.user.
findings.consequence: Any logged-in user can read the total and discount code of every other user's order. They only need to iterate order ids.
findings.fix: Add owner=request.user to the get_object_or_404 lookup, as redeem already does.

findings.title: Decimal multiplied by float raises TypeError
findings.problem: self.total is a Decimal, and the method multiplies it by the float 0.9. Python raises TypeError for Decimal times float.
findings.consequence: Every valid WELCOME10 redemption crashes with a server error. No customer can ever get the discount.
findings.fix: Multiply by Decimal("0.9") and quantize the result to two decimal places.

findings.title: New model field has no migration
findings.problem: The change adds discount_code to Order but adds no migration. orders/migrations holds only 0001_initial, which lacks that column.
findings.consequence: Every Order query selects the missing column and fails with a database error. This breaks the existing order_list view too.
findings.fix: Run makemigrations for the orders app and commit the generated migration that adds discount_code.

findings.title: CSRF protection disabled on session-authenticated POST
findings.problem: redeem changes order state through a POST that relies on the session cookie. The csrf_exempt decorator turns off Django's CSRF check for it.
findings.consequence: A third-party site can make a logged-in user's browser redeem codes on their orders. Today the impact is small, but any future code on this view inherits the hole.
findings.fix: Remove csrf_exempt and have clients send the CSRF token with the request.

findings.title: Once-per-order check races under concurrent requests
findings.problem: apply_discount checks discount_code on the in-memory instance and then writes without a lock. Two concurrent redeem requests can both pass the check.
findings.consequence: Each concurrent request takes another 10 percent off, so the discount stacks on one order.
findings.fix: Lock the row with select_for_update inside a transaction. Or use a conditional update filtered on discount_code="".

findings.title: New discount and view behaviour has no test
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for apply_discount, order_detail or redeem. The change adds new branches and endpoints.
findings.consequence: Any test calling apply_discount would have caught the Decimal crash. A test would also have caught the missing owner check.
findings.fix: Add tests for a valid code, an invalid code, a repeat redemption and access by a non-owner.
